title: Microtrial conductor — run log & quick metrics
body:
Purpose: quick personal tracker for small-scale throughput/latency microtrials. Use as scratchpad to capture runs, rough cost math, and immediate ideas to iterate. Not canonical; will extract into a proper sheet if one run looks promising.

Summary table (latest at top):
| date       | run_id   | model | quant | batch | seq | avg_ms | p95_ms | tokens | est $/1k tok | quality (0-10) | note |
|------------|----------|-------|-------|-------|-----|--------|--------|--------|-------------:|---------------:|------|
| 2026-03-08 | mtrial-73| r-7b  | q4_8  | 8     | 256 | 68     | 132    | 12,400 | 0.65         | 7              | kv-cache warm, stray p95 spike at 11:14
| 2026-03-06 | mtrial-69| r-13b | q8    | 1     | 512 | 145    | 210    | 6,100  | 1.12         | 8              | single-request perf, good quality
| 2026-03-01 | mtrial-63| r-7b  | fp16  | 16    | 128 | 54     | 98     | 20,000 | 0.88         | 6              | higher throughput but hallucinates on long prompts

Quick observations:
- kv-cache warm-ups cut avg_ms by ~12-18% (seen consistently across mtrial-63/73). Add consistent prefix caching for prod when seq>128.
- q8 gives better cost but p95 tails increase on heavy concurrency. Need to test q8 + smaller batch sizes.
- batch=16 helps throughput, but quality regressions noticed for few-shot prompts (compare mtrial-63 quality=6 vs single in mtrial-69 quality=8).

Immediate TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Re-run mtrial-73 with batch=4, measure p99 and token-skew (target window 09:00-12:00 PT).
- [ ] Create a small script to annotate requests that experienced >150ms tail for easier traceback (link to traces).
- [ ] Compare q4_8 vs q5_8 on r-7b for one-shot prompt set (use prompt-set: prompts/one-shot-quality-2026-02).

Flags / open questions:
- Are the p95 spikes correlated with autoscaler activity? Need SRE trace correlation (cc Soren).
- How often does prefix-cache eviction occur on our pool? Add telemetry event if missing.

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- If an experiment shows quality drop >1 point but cost delta >20% lower, run user-percept A/B on 1% traffic (safety: holdback to fallback model).
- Keep small experiments single-tenant on dedicated-dev to avoid noisy neighbors.

Sample quick cost calc (for mental math):
- mtrial-73: 12,400 tokens in 1h -> normalize to 1k-tokens units = 12.4 -> est cost = 12.4 * $0.65 = $8.06 (approx)

Historic bookmarks / links:
- baseline runs: github.com/redwood/inference/actions/workflows/baseline-runs
- prompt set: confluence.redwood.ai/PromptEval/one-shot-quality-2026-02

Sign-off/next: leave this as a personal keeper until I extract to shared sheet. Will tidy and add final results for the best config.

-- Olivia
